studies.title: Bring-up: Apertus 1.5 text policy, 70B start-up, multi-set validation
studies.question: Does the NemoRL + NeMo-Gym mcqa stack train Apertus 1.5 (8B and 70B) on Alps?
studies.finding: Yes. The text conversion matches the release (MedQA 59.2 vs 59.8). 70B start-up peaks at ~415-420 GB per node during the HF load, so it host-OOMs with the checkpoint manager on. Async 70B hung when a vLLM engine died during in-flight weight updates, so those are now off. The multi-set validation (MedQA, MedXpertQA, MMLU-Pro health) smoke test passed on 10-07.

studies.title: Apertus 1.5 RL recipe on AlphaMed (256 x 8 per step)
studies.question: Does the Apertus 1.5 recipe (8 rollouts, clip .2/.28, no KL, lr 1e-6) raise MedQA on 8B and 70B?
studies.finding: 70B: MedQA 64.3 → 68.8 at step 40, then a plateau (+4 pt). No weights were saved because checkpointing was off. 8B: dynamic sampling used ~2 batches per step, so the epoch ran out at step 39.

studies.title: Apertus 1.5-8B, AlphaMed-matched (64 x 8, 300 steps): no-think, thinking, pass-rate filtered + KL
studies.question: Does AlphaMed's recipe give Apertus 1.5-8B a real knowledge gain?
studies.finding: No. The +5-6 pt RL-validation gain is the boxed format: ungradeable answers fall from 9.2 % to 0.4 %, while maj@16 stays flat at 64 and medbench is flat. Thinking reaches 64.0 on RL validation (step 250) but medbench is still flat, apart from MMLU-Pro health +4.9 (~3 SE).

studies.title: Llama-3.1-8B control: KL, entropy bonus, dynamic sampling, adaptive entropy
studies.question: Does the pipeline reproduce AlphaMed on its own base model, and what limits the gain?
studies.finding: Control: 60.4 → 71.5 at step 75. Token entropy collapses from 3.6 to 0.33 by step 50, and answer length later collapses too. Dynamic sampling at step 75 is the best trade-off: medbench MedQA 72.3 with IFEval kept. Adaptive entropy (target 0.5) reaches 73.2 at T 0.6, against 75.8 for AlphaMed-8B. A fixed entropy bonus does nothing at 0.001 and diverges at 0.005.

studies.title: 70B thinking + KL (Apertus 1.5) and Llama-3.1-70B
studies.question: Can 70B runs checkpoint on 10 nodes (MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2) and does 70B gain more?
studies.finding: Start-up memory tests from 10-06. Results not written up yet.

studies.title: Six recipes on three test sets (Llama-3.1-8B, --val-multi)
studies.question: Is the gap to AlphaMed-8B real on MedXpertQA and MMLU-Pro health, and does its exact recipe close it?
studies.finding: The gap is real: MedQA 70-72.7, MedXpertQA 16-18.9 and health 60-63, against AlphaMed-8B's 75.9 / 25.0 / 66.9 in the same evaluation. The AlphaMed-faithful recipe does not close it, although faithful step 75 has the best medbench MedQA (73.5).

studies.title: CuratedQA data (174k MCQ from meditronfo_gptoss_v1)
studies.question: Does 9x more MCQ data move MedXpertQA where AlphaMed19K does not?
studies.finding: MedQA 73.6 at step 125 is the best of all val-multi runs, but MedXpertQA stays at 17.6, below the AlphaMed-data runs. Two continuations started 10-08: the full first CuratedQA pass, and CuratedQA followed by AlphaMed.

studies.title: MOOVE consensus-criteria rubric RL (Plumb-4B judge)
studies.question: Does a rubric reward built from MOOVE consensus criteria improve answers without reward hacking?
studies.finding: Llama-3.1-8B goes from .35 to .89 on validation, but it collapses onto one paragraph template and gives an unsafe dog-bite answer (don't wash the wound). Apertus 1.5-8B stays flat (.59 → .64) with low entropy (.76 vs Llama 4.07). 40-step tests with lr 5e-6 and with thinking are done. The length term ranks systems by length (ρ .68/.48 vs .93/.98 without it), so dropping it is proposed.
